title: TaffyGo renderer observation limits
description: The single committed owner of every provisional numeric bound the BIP renderer endpoint enforces. No other file in this component may contain one of these numbers: observation_limits.h declares the field set and the accessors, tools/generate_observation_limits.py turns this file into the generated header the build compiles, and every call site receives an ObservationLimits object it cannot construct a value for. A number that appears in a second file is a defect, not a duplicate.
owner_note: Every value below is a placeholder chosen so the code has a bound at all. None of them is a quality target and none may be quoted as one. The real numbers come from the supported-device floor and the page corpus and are owned by OD-031 in docs/open-decisions.md; SP-04 replaces this file wholesale with measured values, and replacing it is a data change with no code change.

fields.name: snapshot_max_nodes
fields.why: Ceiling on semantic nodes per extraction, shared across every adapter through one BudgetLedger so the total is a real total rather than a per-adapter bound multiplied by the adapter count.

fields.name: snapshot_max_text_bytes
fields.why: Ceiling on page-derived text copied out of the document in one extraction.

fields.name: snapshot_max_total_bytes
fields.why: Ceiling on everything charged during one extraction, text included.

fields.name: snapshot_node_framing_bytes
fields.why: What one semantic node costs in the framing it is encoded into, before its own strings. Charged instead of sizeof(SemanticNode), which is this process's resident cost for a struct whose empty optionals and empty vectors are dozens of bytes here and nothing on either hop out. Charging the struct made snapshot_max_total_bytes mean a different quantity in this process than it means in the browser, which spends the same number on the encoded payload and then compares the same number against graph_payload.size(): a phone read 397 of 658 nodes while 24 KB of a 256 KB budget actually travelled. Derived from the row framing bip_graph_payload_row.cc writes, not measured on a device.

fields.name: snapshot_edge_framing_bytes
fields.why: The same, for one relationship row, before its four identifier strings.

fields.name: snapshot_text_run_framing_bytes
fields.why: The same, for one text run, before its own text.

fields.name: snapshot_list_element_bytes
fields.why: The same, for one element of a closed-vocabulary list: a state, a content signal, an action kind, a source kind, an attribute or a field-evidence row. Each is an enumeration member or a short record on the wire, never the vector element this process holds.

fields.name: snapshot_max_depth
fields.why: Traversal depth ceiling. Every walk in this component is iterative with an explicit stack, so this bounds work rather than call depth.

fields.name: snapshot_deadline_ms
fields.why: Wall-clock ceiling for one extraction. A renderer timeout must produce a bounded failure rather than stall the interface (protocol section 15).

fields.name: snapshot_max_frames
fields.why: One frame per endpoint. The broker assembles the frame tree from browser-owned topology, so this endpoint never reports another frame's content (protocol section 8.1).

fields.name: delta_max_queued_signals
fields.why: Queue depth before the coalescer sheds droppable classes and then invalidates the projection.

fields.name: delta_max_queued_bytes
fields.why: Queue byte budget, charged with the estimated serialized cost of each signal.

fields.name: delta_coalescing_window_ms
fields.why: How long a batching window stays open when no action barrier is held.

fields.name: delta_min_interval_ms
fields.why: Floor between two delta messages, reported in ProtocolLimits and enforced by the publisher.

fields.name: delta_max_coalescing_window_ms
fields.why: Ceiling the renderer clamps a broker-supplied coalescing window to, so a broker defect cannot become a renderer stall.

fields.name: delta_estimated_signal_bytes
fields.why: Charged per queued signal. A signal carries an identity and a class, never a payload, so one figure is accurate enough to bound the queue.

fields.name: delta_max_tracked_cancellations
fields.why: How many cancelled command identifiers the endpoint remembers. A browser that cancels without limit must not be able to grow renderer memory.

fields.name: structured_data_max_block_bytes
fields.why: Applied to one structured-data block before the parser sees it. A page does not get to choose the renderer's peak memory.

fields.name: structured_data_max_json_depth
fields.why: Nesting ceiling for attacker-authored JSON-LD. Deep nesting is the cheapest way to burn renderer stack.

fields.name: structured_data_max_blocks
fields.why: How many structured-data blocks one document may contribute before the rest are named as omitted.

fields.name: structured_data_max_values_per_property
fields.why: How many disagreeing candidates one property may carry. Conflicting evidence is preserved, but not without a bound.

fields.name: forms_max_forms
fields.why: How many form elements one document may contribute.

fields.name: forms_max_controls_per_form
fields.why: How many controls one form may contribute.

fields.name: forms_max_formless_controls
fields.why: How many controls outside any form element the second pass may contribute. A sign-in box with no form element is the common shape, so this pass is not optional.

fields.name: selection_max_text_bytes
fields.why: Ceiling on selected text copied out of the document.

fields.name: selection_max_nodes
fields.why: Ceiling on nodes reported as inside the user's current selection.

fields.name: layout_max_occlusion_probes
fields.why: How many accessibility hit tests one extraction may run. A node past this bound receives no occlusion determination at all, which fails an anti-occlusion precondition closed.

fields.name: layout_min_visible_area_px
fields.why: Below this area a node is treated as not visible. Zero-size and near-zero-size decoys are a documented fixture shape.

fields.name: layout_viewport_margin_px
fields.why: How far outside the visible viewport a node may extend and still count as on-screen. Zero until the corpus says otherwise.

fields.name: content_signal_max_text_scan_bytes
fields.why: How much of one already-bounded text unit the content-signal detector examines. Signal absence is not an assertion that no signal exists, so bounded evidence is preferable to attacker-controlled work.

fields.name: content_signal_min_encoded_blob_chars
fields.why: Minimum contiguous encoding-alphabet run that may be reported as an encoded blob. Short ordinary identifiers must not make the detector fire everywhere.

fields.name: redaction_min_digit_run
fields.why: Length at which a digit run in free text is treated as a high-risk identifier and dropped whole.

fields.name: redaction_max_digit_separators
fields.why: How many spaces, hyphens, or dots a digit run may contain and still match the detector.

fields.name: redaction_min_hex_run
fields.why: Length at which an unbroken hexadecimal run is treated as key material.

fields.name: redaction_min_token_run
fields.why: Length at which a mixed-case alphanumeric run with token punctuation is treated as an authentication token.

fields.name: redaction_min_seed_phrase_words
fields.why: How many consecutive short lowercase alphabetic words constitute a seed-phrase shape.

fields.name: redaction_max_text_scan_bytes
fields.why: How much of one string the pattern detectors examine. The detectors are a second line, so they are bounded rather than exhaustive; not reading a prohibited value is the first line.
